title: EEG connectome-based machine learning predicts depression severity
summary: Regression models on source-reconstructed resting-state EEG connectivity predicted depression scores in three independent datasets (N = 328). Alpha-band connectivity predicted individual scores (r = 0.6, p = 4e-18) with default mode network regions contributing most, and two external validations gave r = 0.52 (N = 53) and r = 0.44 (N = 154).
ai_technology: Connectome-based predictive regression models on EEG functional connectivity
organization: Lebanese Association for Scientific Research; MINDig; Centre Hospitalier Guillaume Regnier; Empenn (IRISA)

evidence.tested: Two external EEG datasets (N = 53 and N = 154) with significant correlations.
evidence.unknown: Moderate correlations, not diagnostic accuracy; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning regression predicted depression severity from EEG connectivity.

source_review.scope: Abstract and author affiliations read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI. Publisher full text not accessed.
